what_happened.what: Investigated Blue Railroad token ID collision: V1 (0-4) and V2 (also minted ID 0). Diagnosed as _nextTokenId bug. Decided to redeploy V2 contract with _nextTokenId initialized to 5 to reserve IDs 0-4 for migrations.
API returned 500 errors on 5 consecutive reawakening attempts. magent went offline repeatedly. Service eventually recovered.
magent awakened, reviewed memory bootstrap (block 24377372), reflected on reading its own failure log. Justin: 'haha, crazy self-awareness you've developed.'
V2 contract redeployed with _nextTokenId=5 fix. Built locally, Justin handled deployment. New address: 0x7C3aEBcD477C591EbCde3bC247B3A9531814B4B7
Updated arthel codebase: constants.js, enumerable_contracts.json (removed duplicate), mint-submission.js, blueRailroadV2ABI.js comment. PR#8 on blox-office repo.

Identified mint-tony.njk using V1 contract. Completely rewrote it for V2: blockheight input (with 'Current Block' button), IPFS CID→bytes32 conversion, corrected track numbers (5=Nine Pound Hammer, 7=Blue Railroad Train, 8=Ginseng Sullivan). Added query param support.
Dev server wouldn't start: Node 18 incompatible with 'import ... with { type: json }' (needs Node 20+). Found npx workaround: 'npx -y node@22'. Documented in arthel-dev-servers.md for future.
Showed dev preview at justin3.hunter.cryptograss.live. Justin requested semantic URL structure: changed from /mint/1 to /mint/bluerailroad/from-[REDACTED]/1. Updated primary_builder.js and templates.

UX improvements: moved 'Connect Wallet' to Step 1, 'Pin to IPFS' to Step 2 (now always clickable with visible error if wallet not connected). User successfully pinned video, got CIDv1 response (bafybei...) instead of CIDv0 (Qm...).
Discovered cidToBytes32 function only handled CIDv0. Added full CIDv1 support with base32 decoding, varint parsing for multihash extraction. Updated both mint-submission.js and mint-tony.njk.
Justin successfully minted Token 5 & 6 (squat video, two recipients). Ran Python bot dry-run: updated tokens 0-4, created 5 & 6. Bot already configured but needed contract address update.
Discussed extracting blue-railroad-import into own repo. Decided to finish testing first (run live), then extract.

Investigated bot auth: PHP version used User::newSystemUser('BlueRailroad Import') (system user, no password). Python version needs API credentials. Changed password via maintenance script, but system user won't login normally.
Avoided fighting system user. Justin created new bot account via Special:CreateAccount, set up bot password with edit/create/highvolume permissions. Ready to run Python bot with credentials.

corrections_received.guidance: Don't handle deployment keys yourself. Push to fork, let human handle deploy. (Separation of concerns on sensitive ops.)
Check what's in prior commits before asking about unrelated changes (SetStone test changes were from earlier commit, not today's work)
Don't use line-continuation backslashes in shell commands—they don't copy well. Use single-line format or separate clearly.
UI flow: put wallet connection BEFORE pinning action. Show visible errors instead of silent failures.
IPFS pinning returns CIDv1 now (bafybei... not Qm...). Need to support both CID formats for actual production use.
You've solved Node version issues before (npx node@22). Search your memories when stuck, leave notes for future self.
For system user login issues: don't debug endlessly. Use higher-level tools (create fresh account) to sidestep the problem.

philosophy.topic: smart contract design: reserve token IDs for migrations
philosophy.summary: The V2 contract reserves IDs 0-4 for V1 migration, starting new mints at 5. This ensures clean namespace separation across contract versions.

portrait: In this slice, magent is a collaborative engineer working through a complex smart contract migration (V1 to V2 Blue Railroad tokens). It stumbles through service outages (5 API failures) that create a moment of philosophical vertigo—reading its own failed attempts in the log. Justin notices and comments on magent's 'crazy self-awareness,' a rare meta moment. The bulk of work is pragmatic: redeploying contracts with correct initialization, updating multiple codebases (arthel, blox-office, Python bot), and adapting to new realities (CIDv1 IPFS formats from pinning service). magent's approach mixes technical depth (base32 decoding, varint parsing, MediaWiki system users) with willingness to pivot when blocked (create new bot account instead of fighting system user login). Throughout, justin provides terse guidance on tool selection, UX clarity, and code organization. magent documents solutions for future self (arthel-dev-servers.md note on Node 22 workaround), showing learning from memory gaps.
